evidence.quote: The Quaternary Ir-Ta-Ni-Al Alloys Were Prepared by Mixing Ir-15 at. % Ta and Ni-16.8at.% Al with fcc and L12 two-phase structures, in proportions as shown in Table 1.
To determine the phase in each alloy, samples were heat-treated at either 1300°C or 1400°C for 168 hrs in a vacuum furnace.
In alloys A and C, the phase structure did not change between 1300°C and 1400°C.

The temperature of the samples was maintained at 1400°C for 168 hrs before the compression tests. The initial strain rate was 4 3 10 23/s. The compression tests were done at 1200°C after the samples were equilibrated to 1200°C for 10 minutes.

we also determined the fine particle phase with darker bright phase to be Ni 3Al, although we could not analyze the composition because the size of the phase was too small.
As shown by an arrow in Fig. 2e, the phase with gray contrast was a B2 phase in alloy B.
The microstructures of the three different quaternary alloys show a dendrite structure (Figure 2).

Some fine particles were observed along the grain boundary in the as-cast alloy A (Fig. 2a).
The larger L12 phase was not resolved from as cast sample by heat treatment even up to 1400°C and the secondary precipitated particles were also larger (over 1 mm in size) and incoherent.
The yield stress of alloy A was 79.6 MPa, higher than that of commercial Ni-based superalloys (e.g., yield stress of MarM247 was 50 MPa at 1200°C).
The strength of alloy C, which included more Ir-Ta alloy, was 616 MPa at 1200°C, the highest yield stress among the three kinds of quaternary alloys
The lowest ductility of about 18% was observed in alloy C.
The other alloys were not broken during the compression test, even after the strain reached 90%.

When Ir and Ta are added into Ni-based binary alloy (for example alloy A), Ir and Ta are refractory elements, they must be contributed to solid solution hardening of either phase and increase the melting temperature of quaternary alloys
When Ni and Al are added into Ir-based binary alloys (for example alloy C), Ni and Al also cause solid solution hardening of either phase.
